The rules of every route

  • A route that a config key turns off answers 404 not_found.
  • With a baseURL list, a request to an origin outside the list answers 421 host_not_allowed before any route. In each rule, baseURL is the entry of the request’s origin.
  • A POST with an Origin header that is not baseURL and not in trustedOrigins answers 403 origin_not_trusted. Two routes are exceptions: Apple’s form post callback, and the token endpoint, which states its own rule.
  • A failure answers { "error": "<code>" } with the status of the code. hook_refused also carries message, as does the invalid_body of an SSO or SCIM manager write. not_ready also carries reason, and sso_required carries detail.
  • A request body past the cap of its route answers 413 body_too_large, and no parse runs. The cap is 65536 bytes, except 262144 bytes for POST /social/apple/callback, and 8388608 bytes for POST /sso/connections/create and POST /sso/connections/update. A JSON body nested deeper than 16 or with more than 4096 items outside its strings answers 400 invalid_body, and no parse runs. A form body of more than 128 pairs gets the refusal of a bad form of its route, and no parse runs. The SCIM routes answer their own SCIM 413 past 1 MB.
  • The body reads of the routes with a cap above 65536 bytes hold at most 16777216 bytes at once in one isolate. The reads of signed-in users hold at most 8388608 bytes of it, and every other read at most 8388608 bytes. One IP holds at most 4194304 bytes, and so does the one client with no IP. A user may hold the cap of its read, with one large read at a time. A client is its IP before a session and its user after one. A read past that answers 503 body_busy with Retry-After: 1, and no parse runs. The SCIM routes answer their own SCIM 503.
  • Such a read that gets no bytes for 10 s answers 408 body_timeout. So does a read that runs past the time of its cap at 131072 bytes per second, at least 10 s. For a signed-in user the rate is 262144 bytes per second. No parse runs. The SCIM routes answer their own SCIM 408.
  • An unhandled error answers 500 internal and writes one log line.
  • An OPTIONS preflight from a trusted origin answers 204 with the CORS headers. A preflight from another origin answers 403, except where a route states its own rule.
  • Every answer to a trusted origin carries the CORS headers with credentials.
  • The Errors cell of a route does not repeat not_found, origin_not_trusted, and internal, the codes of the router. A route also answers not_found for a record that it names and does not find.
  • The Needs cell names each credential form that the route takes. “A session cookie, or a ts_ bearer token” is a session in either form.

Sessions

POST /sign-out

Field Value
Needs Nothing; or a session cookie, or a ts_ bearer token. A call with no session answers too
Input None
Answer { ok: true }
Errors impersonation_session

POST /magic-link/request

Field Value
Needs Nothing
Input JSON { email, next? }
Answer { sent: true }
Errors invalid_body, rate_limited, captcha_required, captcha_failed, captcha_unavailable

GET /magic-link/verify

Field Value
Needs Nothing. The token of the link is the credential
Input Query { token }
Answer A redirect
Errors invalid_token

POST /tokens

Field Value
Needs A session cookie, or a ts_ bearer token. The session is fresh, and the address is verified
Input JSON { name, expiresInDays?, organizationId?, permissions?, metadata? }
Answer { token, apiToken }
Errors unauthorized, session_not_fresh, invalid_body, email_unverified, rate_limited, token_limit, impersonation_session, forbidden_rank, anonymous_refused

GET /tokens/current

Field Value
Needs A tk_ bearer token
Input None
Answer { token }
Errors unauthorized, rate_limited, token_exhausted, token_retired, conflict

POST /oauth/revoke

Field Value
Needs Nothing; or the client id and secret as HTTP Basic
Input Form { token, client_id?, client_secret?, client_assertion_type?, client_assertion? }
Answer An empty 200
Errors invalid_request, invalid_client, rate_limited, unauthorized_client
